message.content:
**A) Agenda**

**Q1 (λ).** Keep λ = 1 fixed and amend §3. The reason is not that fixed beats nested by 9 pp (−8.7 ± 5.5 by block bootstrap is not evidence of anything); it is that the inner CV is structurally unable to choose λ: with 9–13 episode blocks it picks λ 30–100 in every pre-1990 window, i.e. it selects a near-degenerate model, and the 11 designs span +18.0…+23.4 %. A one-covariate standardised logit on n ≥ 267 is barely sensitive to λ anyway (P 15.1 / 15.8 / 18.2 at λ = 1 / 3 / 30). Post hoc acceptability: yes — λ = 1 is the incumbent, the preregistered interval for nested held, and the only new information is that selection is unreliable. Headline from 2027: **the oracle-free fixed-λ figure (+20.4 %, refit ≈ +17 %)**, because it is the only number a live reader could have obtained; +27.1 and nested +18.3 are printed beside it as "full-origin" and "selector sensitivity". Opus's D1 keeps +27.1 as headline; I don't — it uses labels unknown at the origin.

**Q2 (selection, gate).** Amend §4: no per-origin selector is run; curve-only is operational by council decision. The evidence is unambiguous: the inner-CV advantage of F5 has r = −0.16 with its realised advantage, 76 % of it comes from six 1947–48 rows, and every selector loses 9–10 pp. Gate from 2027: two tiers as in D2, but computed on the *common* origin set, and F5's start-sensitivity (E3: +23.2 / −0.7 / +3.7 %) must be printed in the same line — a benchmark whose sign flips when 24 pre-GS10 quarters are removed is not a benchmark, it is a sensitivity plot. The 4.42 pp tier is an agenda trigger only; the 21 pp tier is the only one that may be called "evidence".

**Q3 (frequency).** Switch to the monthly fit. The preregistered object is the blueprint text; the code thinning was an implementation error, and the general rule "spec governs code when they conflict" is outcome-independent and must be written down as such. The literal reading passes in 6/6 cells, the code reading fails by 0.02 pp in the one phase that happens to coincide with quarterly origins. The monthly fit also matches the live input (a trailing-month reading fitted to monthly history, not to quarter-end snapshots), and the P difference today is 0.5 pp. Conditions: episode-block bootstrap stays the band; the 591 overlapping windows are never described as 591 observations; skill is reported on both origin grids.

**Q4 (start).** Keep 1947Q2. It is a locked constant; moving it is a choice made knowing it lowers P by 2.5–4.5 pp, in the direction the current readings already point. The β is actually steeper without the Shiller years (−1.41 vs −1.29), so the issue is base rate, not slope. Add a permanent supplementary column: P at 1953Q2 and 1960Q1 starts in every ledger row, unscored.

**Q5 (demotion).** Nothing changes in operation. Document that "5 incumbents pass" is an artefact of the asymmetric rule and that under incumbent-as-challenger both simultaneous and backward elimination end at curve-only — read jointly with E3 and E1, this is the strongest evidence that realrate/dd/d_infl/cape_pct are noise. Any future search: one bar in both directions, ≥ +2/+2 pp, ≥ 7/8 LOEO folds, sign stable, fixed in the sealed spec. cape_pct (+4.11/+2.37, 5/8 folds) is explicitly recorded as "not demoted, not confirmed".

**Q6 (content trigger).** Reject. Mean |ΔP| 0.13 pp, max 1.05 pp, below the 1-decimal rounding of P in 90 % of months; against that, 18 data-dependent refits per 49 years, each a new manifest and a discontinuity the ledger key's replay (E5) does not model (it assumes September refits with frozen rounded weights). A preregistered schedule should not become label-dependent for a tenth of a percentage point. Record the 0–9-month lag as a known, bounded property.

**Q7 (ledger key).** Do not amend the scored key. Publish E5 as a supplement with all three censoring variants, the logged-vs-realised base rate (22.8 % vs 15.3 %) and pooled ex post +21.2 %. Public statement, verbatim: "The ledger requires ≈130 years of scored rows (≈150 calendar years) to distinguish the model from the base rate at 80 % power under realistic clustering; naive tests that claim significance after 5–20 years reject a true null 36–53 % of the time. The ledger exists to make each forecast auditable, not to validate the model." Additive change only (no scored row touched): see Q10 item 4.

**Q8 (EBP/Baa).** Close Baa now — a non-redistributable local file is incompatible with a reproducible protocol, full stop. Defer EBP with a hard condition: ≥ 12 monthly snapshots with |revision| < 0.05 at all lags, after which a sealed spec must precommit sign, magnitude (≥ +4.4 pp on common origins) and the admission that the 1990/2001 values have been seen, so only post-2027 behaviour counts as a test. With ~3 usable onsets, expect the answer to be "never admitted"; say so in advance.

**Q9 (L_R).** All announcements, L_R = 21. D9's logic is wrong: the label is the onset, but *censoring* is determined by whether the origin lies between peak and trough. In 1980Q4–1981Q1 an origin is "censored" or "label 0/1" depending on a trough announced 20–21 months later. Eligibility must guarantee that label *and* censoring status are final at R; peak-only does not. Cost: three fewer eligible quarters — acceptable.

**Q10 (F29).** Ratify individually: (1) trailing-month daily DGS10 − DTB3 — yes, provided the monthly GS10 − TB3MS P stays logged in every row; (2) tripwires out of ignition — yes, it restores R3; (3) log day — yes, already in the key; (4) live censoring inside an announced recession — ratify *with* an unscored supplementary column recording P and outcome for censored months. E5 shows this exact rule removes the entire 1980–81 run-up and costs 4.5 pp of replay skill; the double-dip is the case where the live model matters most, and discarding it silently is the one F29 change that was not merely operational.

**B) Verdict on the draft**

- D1 keep, amend headline to oracle-free fixed-λ.
- D2 keep, add common-origin computation and mandatory F5 start-sensitivity line.
- D3 **strike** — monthly fit, spec-governs-code rule written down.
- D4 keep, add unscored three-start column.
- D5 keep, specify the symmetric bar numerically.
- D6 **strike** — no content trigger.
- D7 keep, add the verbatim power statement and the supplementary censored-row column.
- D8 amend: close Baa, defer EBP with the snapshot criterion and precommitted sign/magnitude.
- D9 **strike** — all announcements, L_R = 21.
- D10 amend: ratify 1–3 as written, 4 only with the supplementary logging.

**C) Biggest risk in my proposal**

Q3. I invoke "spec governs code" after seeing that the spec reading passes and the code reading fails. Had the signs been reversed I would like to believe I would still argue spec governs code — but Rasmus should not take my word for it, and neither should I. The honest mitigation is to adopt the precedence rule *as a general protocol clause* applying to every future spec/code conflict regardless of direction, and to publish the quarterly walk-forward in parallel for the life of the model so that the 2.19 pp (CI excluding zero only on overlapping windows) can be seen to persist or evaporate. If the council finds that rule too convenient, I would rather keep quarterly than adopt monthly on a selective principle.
message.reasoning:
I need to draft a roughly 1200-word response as the senior macro-econometrician persona, working through Q1–Q10 with a clear verdict on D1–D10 and identifying the biggest risk, making sure to push back where Opus's positions seem weak rather than just agreeing. Starting with Q1 on the fixed versus nested lambda specification, I'm noting the nested version loses about 9 percentage points, concentrated mainly in the 1970s–80s period.

The deeper issue is whether picking λ=1 after seeing it outperforms nested by 9 points counts as post hoc reasoning — but since λ=1 is inherited from v4 and the preregistered ablation held for the nested range, I lean toward treating λ=1 as the legitimate incumbent rather than a cherry-picked choice. I'm working through whether the honest headline number should be the fixed-λ result or something closer to what an a priori selector would have chosen, concluding that since the shrinkage barely matters at n=267 on a standardized covariate, the 9-point gap is really an artifact of degenerate λ values in early windows near the base rate rather than a meaningful methodological flaw — so I'm siding with D1, though I'm still weighing exactly how to frame the headline effect size.

Ultimately I land on preferring the oracle-free walk-forward figure at fixed λ as the headline, since it's the only number that's genuinely live-publishable, while presenting the full-origin and nested figures as supporting context — this also means clarifying what "oracle-free" actually means given the discrepancy in origin counts (219 vs 198), likely reflecting origins where labels would have been known in real time.

On the gate question, I think the borrowed 4.42 threshold is arbitrary and the own MDE of 21pp effectively neuters the gate so it rarely fires. The two-tier design is workable but I'd flag that the start-sensitivity issue makes the whole benchmark somewhat fragile, which is worth stating plainly.

On frequency, I'd push back on keeping quarterly since full monthly outperforms it by over 2 points.

There's a deeper conflict though: the blueprint text gates the monthly model on its own full monthly walk-forward, but the ablation3 code actually gated on a quarter-thinned score instead — a 0.02 pp discrepancy that's basically noise but still a real mismatch. Since the blueprint is the preregistered document and the code is just the implementation, I think the text should govern when they disagree, even though Opus argues for sticking with the status quo code behavior.

I settle on going with the monthly fit, reasoning that text-governs-code is a general meta-rule rather than an outcome-dependent pick, and that 591 overlapping origins with episode-block bootstrapping give calibrated weights without real detriment. I note the ordering concern — that either choice could look post hoc — but conclude the precedence rule still applies prospectively, so I'll flag the monthly choice accordingly.

On Q4, I confirm keeping 1947Q2 since moving it would shift P downward by 2.5–4.5 points, which itself would be post hoc in the direction of a lower result — so retaining it is the more defensible call.

For Q5, I agree with the demotion decision, but want to flag that F5 should be labeled a survivor of the asymmetric rule, and that E4's curve-only outcome under both procedures actually strengthens the case (alongside E3) that the four extra features are noise. I'd propose a symmetric bar instead: both directions need ≥+2/+2 pp and ≥7/8 folds.

For Q6, I'm weighing the content-trigger adoption — the effects are small (mean |ΔP| of 0.13 pp, max 1.05 pp, 18 extra refits), but each refit creates a new manifest and more ledger discontinuities, adding complexity and making refit timing data-dependent.

Thinking through it as a skeptical econometrician, the payoff here is too marginal — 0.13 pp mean is below P's rounding precision, and introducing data-dependent refit timing into a preregistered September+hash schedule undermines auditability since E5's replay assumed frozen September refits. I'll reject D6 and keep the fixed schedule, noting this is a genuine point of disagreement.

For Q7, I don't think the ledger key should be amended — better to publish a supplement and state honestly that the power is "150 years." But the censoring issue is real: during August 1980–May 1981, the live open-episode rule would have censored readings inside the unannounced 1980 recession (trough not confirmed until July 1981), dropping the 1981 onset's positive rows. Since F29's live censoring rule would do the same thing in real time, this links Q7 to Q10 — the rule costs roughly 4.5 pp of scoreable skill historically and strips out exactly the double-dip cases that matter most.

Rather than ratifying the censoring as "no row," I'd log those rows with a flag marking them as inside an announced recession and score them both ways. The preregistration says rows are never edited, so adding this prospectively could count as an amendment — but I think the resolution is to keep the scoring key untouched and instead add an unscored supplementary column for censored months, which is purely additive and doesn't disturb any already-scored rows. On power, I'd state plainly that the ledger needs roughly 130 years of scored rows to reject the base rate at 80% power, and that its real purpose is auditability of forecasts, not model validation.

For Q8 on EBP/Baa, I'd close out Baa now since it's non-redistributable and violates reproducibility, while deferring EBP pending a revision audit with a hard close date of September 2027 if the audit isn't done — plus noting that since onset values are already observed, only a prospective test is clean, and with just 3 onsets per 30 years that's nearly hopeless, so I'd set it up with 12 snapshots and a sealed precommitted spec on sign and magnitude.

For Q9 on L_R, I'm working through the real-time labeling floor — positive labels at origin require an onset within the next one to four periods.

Actually, this makes me reconsider — if censoring status also depends on the trough, then peak-only eligibility is flawed since an origin's censored-vs-labeled status isn't truly final until the trough is known too. That pushes me toward using all announcements, raising L_R to 21 and shrinking the eligible set by three quarters, which puts me at odds with D9's peak-only framing.

Moving to Q10, I want to ratify each item individually: the trailing-month daily figure (yes, given the data advantage), the swarm tripwires removed from ignition (yes, restores R3), the log-day requirement (yes, it's in the key), and live censoring inside announced recessions (yes, but paired with supplementary unscored logging, acknowledging E5's finding that this costs 4.5pp and drops 1981-type rows). On the overall verdict across D1–D10, I'm keeping D1 as an amendment to the headline and amending D2 for benchmark fragility.

I'll strike D3 in favor of a monthly approach, keep D4 and D5, strike D6, amend D7 and D8, strike D9, and amend D10. The biggest risk in this proposal is the monthly switch itself — I'm worried I'm only invoking "text governs code" because the text reading happened to pass, which raises consistency concerns, plus there's the issue of overlapping windows. I'll flag that as the primary risk to address and aim for a tight write-up around 1200 words.
